# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, cut_partial, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked,
                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)
assumptions: Temperature and vibration are readings; averaged across sensors per period.

            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).

    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""

                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:

            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, cut_partial, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked,
                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""

                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)

    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]

    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column

            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")

                return None

                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why

                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue

            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)

            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")

                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:

                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue

                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]

                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):

                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Anomaly detection on mrr
    col = 'mrr'
    vals = df[col].dropna()
    skew = float(vals.skew())
    if abs(skew) > 2:
        shift = max(0, -vals.min() + 1)
        work = np.log1p(vals + shift)
    else:
        shift = 0
        work = vals.copy()

    q1, q3 = work.quantile(0.25), work.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo3, hi3 = q1 - 3 * iqr, q3 + 3 * iqr
    lo4, hi4 = q1 - 4 * iqr, q3 + 4 * iqr
    lo5, hi5 = q1 - 5 * iqr, q3 + 5 * iqr

    extreme_mask = (work < lo3) | (work > hi3)
    extreme_frac = extreme_mask.sum() / len(work)

    if extreme_frac > 0.05:
        result['anomalies'].append({
            "column": col,
            "row_index": None,
            "value": None,
            "expected_range": f"{float(np.expm1(lo3) - shift):.2f} – {float(np.expm1(hi3) - shift):.2f}" if abs(skew) > 2 else f"{float(lo3):.2f} – {float(hi3):.2f}",

                lo_orig = float(lo3)

            if v_work > hi5 or v_work < lo5:
                sev = "critical"
            elif v_work > hi4 or v_work < lo4:
                sev = "high"
            else:
                sev = "medium"
            exp_range = f"{lo_orig:.2f} – {hi_orig:.2f}"
            result['anomalies'].append({
                "column": col,
                "row_index": int(idx),
                "value": v_orig,
                "expected_range": exp_range,
                "severity": sev,
                "explanation": f"Value {v_orig} lies outside expected range {exp_range} for column {col}."
            })
except Exception:
    pass

        first_val = float(monthly_mrr['mrr'].iloc[0])
        last_val = float(monthly_mrr['mrr'].iloc[-1])
        pct = (last_val - first_val) / first_val * 100 if first_val != 0 else 0.0
        direction = "up" if pct > 1 else ("down" if pct < -1 else "flat")
        result['trends'].append({
            "column": "mrr",
            "period": "MoM",
            "direction": direction,
            "pct_change": round(pct, 4),
            "segment": None
        })
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Forecasting: simple linear extrapolation of MRR for next 3 months
    monthly_mrr2 = (
        df[df['in_force_now'] == 'yes']
        .groupby(pd.Grouper(key='month', freq='MS'))['mrr']
        .sum()
        .reset_index()
        .sort_values('month')
    )
    if len(monthly_mrr2) >= 3:
        x = np.arange(len(monthly_mrr2))
        y = monthly_mrr2['mrr'].values
        slope, intercept, _, _, _ = stats.linregress(x, y)
        last_month = monthly_mrr2['month'].iloc[-1]
        for i in range(1, 4):
            future_month = last_month + pd.DateOffset(months=i)
            pred = float(intercept + slope * (len(monthly_mrr2) - 1 + i))
            result['forecast_points'].append({
                "period": future_month.strftime("%Y-%m"),
                "value": round(pred, 2)
            })
        result['assumptions'].append(f"Forecast uses OLS linear trend on monthly MRR snapshots (slope={slope:.2f}/month).")
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Statistical test: one-way ANOVA on mrr by plan (in-force)
    groups = [g['mrr'].dropna().values for _, g in in_force.groupby('plan') if len(g) >= 5]
    if len(groups) >= 2:
        f_stat, p_val = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
        interp = (
            f"One-way ANOVA on mrr by plan: F={f_stat:.3f}, p={p_val:.3g}. "
            + ("Significant difference in MRR across plans." if p_val < 0.05 else "No significant difference in MRR across plans.")
        )
        result['statistical_tests'].append({
            "test_name": "One-way ANOVA: mrr by plan",
            "statistic": float(f_stat),
            "p_value": float(p_val),
            "interpretation": interp
        })
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Statistical test: one-way ANOVA on mrr by segment (in-force)
    groups_seg = [g['mrr'].dropna().values for _, g in in_force.groupby('segment') if len(g) >= 5]
    if len(groups_seg) >= 2:
        f2, p2 = stats.f_oneway(*groups_seg)
        interp2 = (
            f"One-way ANOVA on mrr by segment: F={f2:.3f}, p={p2:.3g}. "
            + ("Significant difference in MRR across segments." if p2 < 0.05 else "No significant difference in MRR across segments.")
        )
        result['statistical_tests'].append({
            "test_name": "One-way ANOVA: mrr by segment",
            "statistic": float(f2),
            "p_value": float(p2),
            "interpretation": interp2
        })
except Exception:
    pass

gaps: The analysis covers aggregate MRR trends and retention metrics but does not examine customer acquisition cost, lifetime value, or payback period, which would contextualize whether the 20.1% logo churn and 91.1% net revenue retention are sustainable.

No breakdown of churn or expansion by cohort (e.g., customers acquired in each month) is shown, which would reveal whether retention or expansion patterns differ by customer age or acquisition period.
The dataset does not include reasons for churn, contraction, or expansion, so the drivers behind the 20.1% logo churn and the Mar 2026 spike cannot be identified from the data alone.
next_investigations: Analyze MRR movement by customer cohort (acquisition month) to determine whether newer customers have higher churn or lower expansion rates than established customers, and whether the 20.1% logo churn is concentrated in specific cohorts.

Compare the Mar 2026 Enterprise customer churn event to other months to identify whether similar concentration risk (one customer >80% of monthly churn) exists in the current paying base or has recurred.

Decompose the 91.1% net revenue retention into expansion and contraction by plan and segment to identify which tiers are driving the gap between gross (77.2%) and net retention, and whether Growth-plan expansion can offset Starter and Scale contraction.
methodology_concerns: Logo churn (20.1%) is measured only on the 12-month cohort to 31 Oct 2026 with no full year-earlier window in the data, limiting the ability to compare churn rates across periods or assess whether churn is accelerating or stabilizing.

The MRR bridge components (new, expansion, reactivation, contraction, churned) are computed from month-end snapshots; customers who join and leave within a single month are invisible, potentially understating true churn activity.

Segmentation and trend analyses use only in_force_now='yes' rows to reflect current paying customers, while the EDA summary covers all rows as loaded (including historical snapshots), which may create inconsistency in how totals and averages are interpreted.

    result['assumptions'].append("Only one numeric column (mrr); no pairwise correlations beyond target pairs.")
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Anomaly detection on mrr
    col = 'mrr'
    vals = df[col].dropna()
    skew = float(vals.skew())
    if abs(skew) > 2:
        shift = max(0, -vals.min() + 1)
        work = np.log1p(vals + shift)
    else:
        shift = 0
        work = vals.copy()

    q1, q3 = work.quantile(0.25), work.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo3, hi3 = q1 - 3 * iqr, q3 + 3 * iqr
    lo4, hi4 = q1 - 4 * iqr, q3 + 4 * iqr
    lo5, hi5 = q1 - 5 * iqr, q3 + 5 * iqr

    extreme_mask = (work < lo3) | (work > hi3)
    extreme_frac = extreme_mask.sum() / len(work)

    if extreme_frac > 0.05:
        result['anomalies'].append({
            "column": col,
            "row_index": None,
            "value": None,
            "expected_range": f"{float(np.expm1(lo3) - shift):.2f} – {float(np.expm1(hi3) - shift):.2f}" if abs(skew) > 2 else f"{float(lo3):.2f} – {float(hi3):.2f}",
            "severity": "low",
            "explanation": f"Column {col} has heavy-tailed distribution ({extreme_frac*100:.1f}% of values outside 3×IQR boundary); not flagged individually."
        })
    else:
        extreme_idx = work[extreme_mask].index.tolist()[:25]
        for idx in extreme_idx:
            v_work = work.loc[idx]
            v_orig = float(df.loc[idx, col])
            if abs(skew) > 2:
                lo_orig = float(np.expm1(lo3) - shift)
                hi_orig = float(np.expm1(hi3) - shift)
            else:
                lo_orig = float(lo3)
                hi_orig = float(hi3)
            if v_work > hi5 or v_work < lo5:
                sev = "critical"
            elif v_work > hi4 or v_work < lo4:
                sev = "high"
            else:
                sev = "medium"
            exp_range = f"{lo_orig:.2f} – {hi_orig:.2f}"
            result['anomalies'].append({
                "column": col,
                "row_index": int(idx),
                "value": v_orig,
                "expected_range": exp_range,
                "severity": sev,
                "explanation": f"Value {v_orig} lies outside expected range {exp_range} for column {col}."
            })
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Trend: MRR over time using in-force snapshot per month
    monthly_mrr = (
        df[df['in_force_now'] == 'yes']
        .groupby(pd.Grouper(key='month', freq='MS'))['mrr']
        .sum()
        .reset_index()
        .sort_values('month')
    )
    if len(monthly_mrr) >= 2:
        first_val = float(monthly_mrr['mrr'].iloc[0])
        last_val = float(monthly_mrr['mrr'].iloc[-1])
        pct = (last_val - first_val) / first_val * 100 if first_val != 0 else 0.0
        direction = "up" if pct > 1 else ("down" if pct < -1 else "flat")
        result['trends'].append({
            "column": "mrr",
            "period": "MoM",
            "direction": direction,
            "pct_change": round(pct, 4),
            "segment": None
        })
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Forecasting: simple linear extrapolation of MRR for next 3 months
    monthly_mrr2 = (
        df[df['in_force_now'] == 'yes']
        .groupby(pd.Grouper(key='month', freq='MS'))['mrr']
        .sum()
        .reset_index()
        .sort_values('month')
    )
    if len(monthly_mrr2) >= 3:
        x = np.arange(len(monthly_mrr2))
        y = monthly_mrr2['mrr'].values
        slope, intercept, _, _, _ = stats.linregress(x, y)
        last_month = monthly_mrr2['month'].iloc[-1]
        for i in range(1, 4):
            future_month = last_month + pd.DateOffset(months=i)
            pred = float(intercept + slope * (len(monthly_mrr2) - 1 + i))
            result['forecast_points'].append({
                "period": future_month.strftime("%Y-%m"),
                "value": round(pred, 2)
            })
        result['assumptions'].append(f"Forecast uses OLS linear trend on monthly MRR snapshots (slope={slope:.2f}/month).")
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Statistical test: one-way ANOVA on mrr by plan (in-force)
    groups = [g['mrr'].dropna().values for _, g in in_force.groupby('plan') if len(g) >= 5]
    if len(groups) >= 2:
        f_stat, p_val = stats.f_oneway(*groups)
        interp = (
            f"One-way ANOVA on mrr by plan: F={f_stat:.3f}, p={p_val:.3g}. "
            + ("Significant difference in MRR across plans." if p_val < 0.05 else "No significant difference in MRR across plans.")
        )
        result['statistical_tests'].append({
            "test_name": "One-way ANOVA: mrr by plan",
            "statistic": float(f_stat),
            "p_value": float(p_val),
            "interpretation": interp
        })
except Exception:
    pass

try:
    # Statistical test: one-way ANOVA on mrr by segment (in-force)
    groups_seg = [g['mrr'].dropna().values for _, g in in_force.groupby('segment') if len(g) >= 5]
    if len(groups_seg) >= 2:
        f2, p2 = stats.f_oneway(*groups_seg)
        interp2 = (
            f"One-way ANOVA on mrr by segment: F={f2:.3f}, p={p2:.3g}. "
            + ("Significant difference in MRR across segments." if p2 < 0.05 else "No significant difference in MRR across segments.")
        )
        result['statistical_tests'].append({
            "test_name": "One-way ANOVA: mrr by segment",
            "statistic": float(f2),
            "p_value": float(p2),
            "interpretation": interp2
        })
except Exception:
    pass

result['assumptions'].append("Segmentation and trends use in_force_now=='yes' rows to reflect current paying customers.")
result['assumptions'].append("EDA summary covers all rows as loaded (including historical snapshots).")
result['assumptions'].append("Anomaly detection applied to all mrr rows; log1p transform used if |skew|>2.")

# built-in statistics, computed in-process (agents/analysis_agent.standard_stats)
def standard_stats(raw: dict, df: pd.DataFrame, contract: DataContract, task: AnalysisTask) -> None:
    """Statistics with one right answer, computed in this process with the shared functions (plan
    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, cut_partial, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked,
                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,

    v2 R2: they were a second copy of the rules, as code text run in the sandbox, and drifted).
    Merged into the sandbox's `raw` result as before: a target's MoM (and YoY on a pack's data)
    replaces the model's; target-pair r and the joint breakdown fill gaps; a level by segment
    replaces only the model's totals and means of it. Ids go to raw['builtin'] (evidence)."""
    from agents.utils import (LevelUnavailable, aggregate, cut_partial, effective_agg, latest_rows, pct_change, ranked,
                              time_axis, weekly_cadence)
    from domain_pack import entity_rows, rows_for
    types = {t.value if hasattr(t, "value") else t for t in task.analysis_types}
    names = set(df.columns)
    targets = [c for c in task.target_metrics if c in contract.metric_columns and c in names]
    segs = [c for c in task.segments if c in names]
    # a column's summary over the rows its tiles count (a claim's replaced and voided versions
    # out, as every answer and chart): replaces the sandbox's every-row summary of that column
    for c in (c for c in contract.metric_columns if c in names):
        if (summary := counted_summary(df, contract, c)) is not None:
            raw.setdefault("eda_summary", {})[c] = summary
    for key, empty in (("builtin", []), ("correlations", {}), ("trends", []), ("segments", []),
                       ("assumptions", [])):
        raw.setdefault(key, empty)
    level = {c.name for c in contract.columns if c.aggregation in ("last", "first")}

    if types & {"correlation", "hypothesis"}:   # snapshot data: one row per entity
        cdf = entity_rows(df, contract)
        for i, a in enumerate(targets):
            for b in targets[i + 1:]:
                if f"{a}__{b}" in raw["correlations"] or f"{b}__{a}" in raw["correlations"]:
                    continue
                r = pd.to_numeric(cdf[a], errors="coerce").corr(pd.to_numeric(cdf[b], errors="coerce"))
                if r == r:
                    raw["correlations"][f"{a}__{b}"] = round(float(r), 4)
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"corr:{a}__{b}")

    yoy = defaults_pack(contract) is not None
    if types & {"trend", "forecasting"} and targets:
        replaced = ("MoM", "YoY") if yoy else ("MoM",)
        raw["trends"] = [t for t in raw["trends"] if not (isinstance(t, dict) and t.get("period")
                         in replaced and t.get("column") in targets)]

        def monthly(col: str):
            """(rows, their month, how a month is made) for `col`, judged once on the whole file:
            the rows its tiles count, the main currency and a mid-month export's partial last
            month (a segment's slice never re-judges them)."""
            date = time_axis(contract, col, df)
            agg = effective_agg(contract, col, None) or (
                "mean" if pd.to_numeric(df[col], errors="coerce").dropna().between(0, 1).all() else "sum")
            if not date or (agg in ("last", "first") and col not in level):
                return None
            rows, m = counted_months(df, contract, col, date)
            t = pd.to_datetime(rows[date], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            weeks = t.groupby(m).nunique() if yoy and agg == "sum" and weekly_cadence(t) else None
            return rows.assign(_m=m), agg, weeks

        def series_of(rows: pd.DataFrame, col: str, agg: str, weeks):
            """Calendar-month values: a level's month-ends, a flow's totals (a rate's means); weekly
            data: each month is its average week."""
            try:
                out = aggregate(rows[rows["_m"].notna()], ["_m"], col, agg, contract,
                                over_time=True).sort_index()
            except LevelUnavailable:   # a level without its account column: no built-in trend
                return None
            if weeks is not None:
                out = out / weeks.reindex(out.index)
                note = "Weekly data: each month is compared as its average week (months have 4 or 5 week-endings)."
                if note not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
            return out.dropna()

        for c in targets:
            made = monthly(c)
            if made is None:
                continue
            rows, agg, weeks = made
            overall = series_of(rows, c, agg, weeks)
            if overall is None or len(overall) < 2:
                continue
            # a measure that develops (losses at a valuation): a change between young accident
            # months is development, not a trend; no built-in MoM / YoY, the note says why
            if note := developing_trend(contract, df, c):
                if (note := f"{c}:{note}") not in raw["assumptions"]:
                    raw["assumptions"].append(note)
                continue
            # the data's own last month (before partial / run-out months were left out)
            data_last = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed",
                                       errors="coerce").dt.to_period("M").max()
            # every segment compares the same months as the whole file (never its own last two,
            # which can be a stale pair); a flow's month with no rows is 0
            last = overall.index[-1]
            # a first month the data covers only part of (invoices from 26 Sep) is no month to
            # compare with: utils.cut_partial, the one rule (Domain 6 live run: '+109% YoY'
            # against five days of September)
            dated = pd.to_datetime(rows[time_axis(contract, c, df)], format="mixed", errors="coerce")
            kept, _ = cut_partial(overall, dated, "M")
            partial_first = overall.index[0] if len(kept) and kept.index[0] != overall.index[0] else None
            pairs = [(k, p_) for k, p_ in (("MoM", overall.index[-2]), ("YoY", last - 12 if yoy else None))
                     if p_ != partial_first]
            jobs = [(None, overall, rows)]
            if segs:   # the 10 largest groups, ties by name (the same on every machine)
                for v in ranked(df[segs[0]].value_counts()).head(10).index:
                    part = rows[rows[segs[0]] == v]
                    series = series_of(part, c, agg, weeks)
                    if series is not None and agg == "sum":
                        series = series.reindex(overall.index, fill_value=0)
                    jobs.append((str(v), series, part))
            for seg, series, part in jobs:
                if series is None:
                    continue
                tag = f"trend:{c}" + (f" ({seg})" if seg else "")
                for period, then in pairs:
                    if then is None or then not in series.index or last not in series.index:
                        continue
                    pct = pct_change(series[last], series[then])
                    if pct is None:
                        continue
                    pct = round(float(pct), 2)   # the direction says the stated figure
                    n = int(part.loc[part["_m"].isin([last, then]), c].notna().sum())
                    named = {"latest": str(last), "previous": str(then)} if last != data_last else {}
                    raw["trends"].append({"column": c, "period": period, "pct_change": pct,
                                          "segment": seg, "n": n, **named,
                                          "direction": "up" if pct > 0 else "down" if pct < 0 else "flat"})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"{tag}:{period}")

    if "segmentation" in types:
        keys = [[x] for x in segs] + ([segs[:2]] if len(segs) >= 2 else [])
        for c in targets:
            rows, _ = rows_for(df, contract, c)
            if c in level:   # a level by segment: each entity's latest row (a closed or stopped
                cur = latest_rows(rows, c, contract)   # account is out), totals and means
                for k in keys:
                    s_ = "|".join(k)
                    raw["segments"] = [x for x in raw["segments"] if not (
                        isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == s_ and x.get("metric_column") == c
                        and str(x.get("aggregation") or "sum").lower() in ("sum", "total", "last", "first",
                                                                             "mean", "avg", "average"))]
                    for agg, vals in (("last", cur.groupby(k)[c].sum(min_count=1).dropna()),
                                      ("mean", cur.groupby(k)[c].mean().dropna())):
                        raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": s_, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": agg,
                                                "results": [{"name": "|".join(map(str, n)) if isinstance(n, tuple)
                                                             else str(n), "value": round(float(v), 4)}
                                                            for n, v in vals.items()]})
                    raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{s_}/{c}")
            elif len(segs) >= 2:   # the joint breakdown fills a gap
                joint = "|".join(segs[:2])
                if any(isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("segment_column") == joint and x.get("metric_column") == c
                       for x in raw["segments"]):
                    continue
                means = rows.groupby(segs[:2])[c].mean()
                top = ranked(rows.groupby(segs[:2]).size()).head(20).index
                raw["segments"].append({"segment_column": joint, "metric_column": c, "aggregation": "mean",
                                        "results": [{"name": f"{a}|{b}", "value": round(float(means[(a, b)]), 4)}
                                                    for a, b in top]})
                raw["builtin"].append(f"seg:{joint}/{c}")
    _drop_protected_cells(raw, df, contract)

anomaly_alerts.title: How these numbers are counted
anomaly_alerts.description: Read as manufacturing data (OEE, availability, performance rate, quality (first-pass yield), MTBF, good count, failures, assets). Ratios pool their parts (OEE and availability over planned production time, summed over shifts and machines before dividing), so a line's figure pools its machines' time; MTBF is run time per failure and assumes a constant failure rate; MTTR runs from actual start to actual finish of finished repairs, so repairs still open are not in it and it can read low. Readings are averaged, not time-weighted. Times are read in the zone they are written in (a file mixing offsets is read in UTC). The data covers 3 months, so month-over-month changes may be seasonal; there is no same month last year to compare with. Operators are people: figures by operator describe the work, never rank the people, and groups of fewer than 11 operators are not shown.

paragraphs.text: The dataset covers 2,630 production runs across 16 columns from August through October 2026, capturing OEE, availability, performance, quality, downtime, and failure metrics.
Unplanned Downtime has been trending upward over the most recent 7-day rolling window, which warrants attention alongside flagged outliers in Scrap Count and Stops.

findings.text: First-pass yield stands at 97.1% and the 7-day rolling Good Count trend is essentially flat at -0.5%, suggesting output quality has been stable across the period.
Unplanned Downtime is trending up +5.0% on a 7-day rolling basis, and it moves together with both Stops and Ideal Cycle Time across runs.
Planned Minutes is the strongest single factor moving with output volume: it moves closely with Total Count and Good Count, and also moves together with Unplanned Downtime.
MTBF is 42.29 hours; note that MTTR figures reflect only completed repairs and may read low because open repairs are excluded.
Planned Minutes and Unplanned Downtime move together in the data: an association, not proof that one causes the other.

    if abs(skew) > 2:
        transformed = np.log1p(rh_s + shift)
    else:
        transformed = rh_s.copy()
    q1, q3 = transformed.quantile(0.25), transformed.quantile(0.75)
    iqr = q3 - q1
    lo3, hi3 = q1 - 3 * iqr, q3 + 3 * iqr
    lo4, hi4 = q1 - 4 * iqr, q3 + 4 * iqr
    lo5, hi5 = q1 - 5 * iqr, q3 + 5 * iqr
    extreme_mask = (transformed < lo3) | (transformed > hi3)

anomaly_alerts.description: Read as manufacturing data (MTTR, corrective work orders, open work orders, assets). Ratios pool their parts (OEE and availability over planned production time, summed over shifts and machines before dividing), so a line's figure pools its machines' time; MTBF is run time per failure and assumes a constant failure rate; MTTR runs from actual start to actual finish of finished repairs, so repairs still open are not in it and it can read low. Readings are averaged, not time-weighted. Times are read in the zone they are written in (a file mixing offsets is read in UTC). Oct 2026 is partial (data through the 24th) and is left out of period comparisons. 39 cancelled work orders are left out of every count and of MTTR. The data covers 5 months, so month-over-month changes may be seasonal; there is no same month last year to compare with. Reporters are people: figures by who reported a work order describe the work, never rank the people, and groups of fewer than 11 people are not shown.
